overall: Atlanta had an unseasonably hot afternoon, with the running daily max already locked in at 91.4°F, recorded around 16:19 ET. Temperatures have since dropped sharply — from 89.6°F at 16:52 to 80.6°F by 17:52 — driven by convective activity, with a severe thunderstorm watch in effect through 11 PM EDT and multiple active warnings across the metro region. The evening is now turning stormy with dewpoints in the low-to-mid 70s and active lightning/wind hazards.

This suggests the models missed the extent of afternoon heating, possibly underestimating the post-frontal mixing and convective cap break that allowed temps to surge briefly past 91°F before storm activity collapsed the boundary layer.
